problem: Sales reps spend time on CRM admin and leaders lack trustworthy pipeline data.
product_category: AI revenue infrastructure, conversation intelligence and CRM automation

founders.name: Yash Dulla
founders.background_notes: Won Stanford hackathon in 2024 per YC page.

founders.name: Ishan Sheth
prior_employers: unnamed startups and a bank (per YC page)
education: Georgia Tech, Computer Science and Economics (per YC page)

competitors.name: Gong
competitors.what: Conversation intelligence with forecasting and deal boards

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingesting calls, email and Slack and writing back to CRM is standard integration engineering; the founders built a first version over a weekend per their launch post.

defensibility.rationale: Historical data backfill and CRM write-back create some lock-in, but incumbents and many startups sell similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Gong added forecasting and deal boards; no acquisition of Ergo found.

market_need_then: The founders cite a customer startup where a first version unlocked $75K in closed contracts; sales teams already paid for Gong and Clari.

identity.visual_style: Abstract node and grid illustrations, cube motif

brand_strength.rationale: Ergo is a common word shared with an Irish IT firm acquired by Presidio and many others, so search is crowded. The joinergo.com domain suggests the exact name was unavailable.

outcome_analysis: Ergo is active with named startup customers and a June 2026 seed round of $2.8M led by FCVC, well after its Winter 2025 batch. Quoted customer results are self-selected, and the press release gives no revenue figures. Incumbent conversation intelligence vendors are the main risk.
notes: Seed confirmed by two press release hosts. Startupintros reports a $500K seed in February 2025 and VCBacked a $500K FundersClub pre-seed; aggregator only, unverified, not recorded. CB Insights lists a Nov 2025 L Squared round that no other source mentions; unverified. Competitor entries come from a 2025 vendor list, so dating is approximate. Ergo is described on its site as backed by FundersClub.
